To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term treatment (2 weeks) with clinically relevant doses of zimelidine, imipramine and desipram-ine produce a reduction in 5-HT synthesis and in 5-HT dependent head twitch behaviour, and a reduction of prolactin release.
long-term antidepressant treatments may reduce the activity of 5-HT synapse in some areas of the brain.
long-term treatment of rats with antidepressants produces a reduction of the number of 5-HT binding sites in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of long-term antidepressant drug treatment in the rat.
the effects of antidepressant drug treatment in the brain of animals and humans.
the study of the effects of chronic antidepressant treatment on central serotonin mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptive changes in the serotonergic system following long-term antidepressant drug treatment are not uniform and may be different for the different drugs and for different brain regions.
long-term treatment in clinically relevant doses with zimelidine and other antidepressant drugs may lead to adaptive changes in 5HT neurotransmission in certain areas of the brain.
the adaptive changes in central serotonergic systems following long-term treatment may be of a complex nature, involving several different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
long-term treatment of rats with antidepressant drugs produces adaptive changes in 5HT synapses in the central nervous system.
the 5-HT uptake inhibitors produce adaptive changes in central 5-HT neurotransmitter systems which may contribute to the clinical efficacy of these drugs in the treatment of depressive disorders.
the effects of antidepressant treatment on the 5-HT system are more pronounced than on other neurotransmitter systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of chronic antidepressant treatment on 5-HT neurotransmitter systems are complex.
there are many different ways to increase serotonin, and they are all associated with different effects on the brain.
there is a lot of variability in how people respond to antidepressants.
